claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms an amorphous phase only under very rapid quenching.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 undergoes rapid crystallization or a complex thermal response during heating.
Adding approximately 2 at.% boron will improve the glass-forming ability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 during rapid solidification.
Adding approximately 2 at.% boron will enhance the alloy's thermal stability during reheating.
The boron should replace a small portion of one transition-metal constituent rather than simply being added to the stated base composition.
Cooling rates on the order of at least 10^4 K/s are suitable for testing the proposed improvement.
Moderate reheating rates would normally trigger crystallization in the base alloy.
The intervention should work only when cooling is sufficiently rapid to produce a largely amorphous initial structure.
The proposed thermal-stability benefit should persist only while reheating remains below the boron-modified alloy's crystallization onset.
Boron atoms have small atomic size and strong covalent-bonding tendencies.
Boron addition will increase local atomic-packing frustration.
Boron addition will disrupt short-range ordering and thereby hinder crystalline-phase nucleation.
Boron addition will increase structural disorder and raise the activation energy for crystallization.
The increased disorder and crystallization barrier will suppress crystalline-nucleus growth during both cooling and reheating.
Suppressing crystallization will produce a more homogeneous glassy structure with delayed crystallization kinetics.
The boron-modified alloy will retain a higher amorphous-phase fraction than the base alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will retain amorphous material over a broader range of cooling rates than the base alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature during reheating than the base alloy.
At cooling rates below approximately 10^3 K/s, the boron-modified alloy may still crystallize.
Heating well above the modified alloy's crystallization threshold may negate the proposed stability enhancement.
